title: ReviewCheck MCP tool contracts
description: Tool contracts for the local MCP server (an add-on running inside the host agent). Reference: docs/13. CONSTRAINTS: (1) every tool that presents a block ALWAYS returns 'code' and 'explanation' together (co-presence, docs/13 §1.1); (2) the explanation is anchored to line citations (grounding, docs/13 §1 2-bis); (3) the review outcome is the SUM of the per-block human decisions (accept/request_correction) + an explicit confirmation: the AI neither judges nor approves (human-in-the-loop, docs/13 §1.2). No backend/DB: the 'session' is a handle to a LOCAL state file (see session-state.schema.json).

Block.description: A unit of intent. code and explanation are both REQUIRED (co-presence). The code is the source of truth; the explanation is anchored to the code (grounding).

code.description: The block's code (diff + minimal context). ALWAYS present. Source of truth.

explanation.description: An explanation that DESCRIBES AND ASKS, never a verdict. Anchored to the code (grounding).

link.description: Edges to related blocks (from the graph's structural facts, not invented)

citations.description: The code lines the explanation is anchored to (grounding).

uncertainty.description: Where the model is uncertain / anchoring is weak; null if absent.

related_block_ids.description: Edges (F3): related blocks, peekable on demand.

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.description: Lists open pull requests for a repo, EXCLUDING ones the authenticated user opened themselves (self-review has no approve/request_changes path — GUARDRAILS G10). Use this to choose which PR to review before calling get_review_plan with source.type='pull_request'. Read-only: no session is opened, nothing is posted.

pull_requests.description: Open PRs, self-authored ones already excluded.

tools.name: get_review_plan
tools.description: Reads the local diff and returns the plan: blocks, reading order, interaction points (seams), and the FIRST complete block (code + explanation). Opens a local session. SOURCE: the LOCAL diff (git, no token/network) — review what the agent/you just wrote. Ref: 'working' (default) | 'staged' | a git range | a commit.

ref.description: 'working' (uncommitted changes, default) | 'staged' | a git range (e.g. 'origin/main...HEAD') | a commit.

session.description: Handle to the local session (state file).

interaction_points.description: Seams to verify (F13), derived from the graph — attention pointers, not verdicts.

notice.description: Optional one-line banner on how the explanations were produced for this review: hosting mode (host model via sampling, grounded), or the deterministic structural narrative (no key / no hosting). The agent shows it once at the top.

is_self_review.description: PR sources only: true if the authenticated identity opened this PR themselves. When true, the agent must tell the user UP FRONT that submit_review can only reach comment_only, never approve/request_changes (GUARDRAILS G10) — not as a surprise at close time. Null for a local review.

tools.name: next_block
tools.description: Advances to the next recommended block and returns it COMPLETE (code + explanation together). The client must print code and explanation together, never on a separate request.

tools.name: get_block
tools.description: Returns a specific block COMPLETE (code + explanation together). Also used to 'peek' at a related block without advancing (F4).

tools.name: accept_block
tools.description: The user ACCEPTS the block (they understood it and take responsibility for it). A human decision recorded in the local state file.

tools.name: request_correction
tools.description: The user REQUESTS A CORRECTION on the block, with a note. Marks the block as 'to correct' and stores the note (it becomes a comment in the request-changes).

tools.name: review_status
tools.description: Session status: position, progress, accepted blocks, and blocks to correct.

tools.name: submit_review
tools.description: Closes the review. The outcome is the SUM of the per-block human decisions (never an AI verdict). Fails if any block is undecided. Behavior depends on the SOURCE: (A) LOCAL (pre-PR): posts NOTHING — returns a summary + a list of corrections to apply; outcome 'ready_to_proceed' (all accepted) or 'corrections_to_apply' (>=1 correction). Here the self-approval problem does not exist. (B) PULL REQUEST: with 'confirm':true, posts ONE review to the platform — 'approve' (all accepted) or 'request_changes' (>=1 correction, posted as inline comments from the reviewer's own notes); without confirm, returns the SAME outcome as a preview and posts nothing. A self-authored PR (is_self_review from get_review_plan) ALWAYS closes as 'comment_only' instead — approve/request_changes are never even attempted (GUARDRAILS G10).

confirm.description: For a pull request source: without confirm, this is a preview only and nothing is posted (GUARDRAILS G6/G8). Ignored for a local review, which never posts.

outcome.description: Local review: ready_to_proceed (all accepted) | corrections_to_apply (≥1 correction). Pull request: approve | request_changes | comment_only (always this last one when is_self_review is true).

posted.description: True only when a pull request review was actually sent to the platform (confirm:true, platform reachable). Always false for the local review, for a preview (confirm:false), or if posting failed — see summary.

notes.description: The requested corrections — an actionable to-do list to apply locally.

undecided_blocks.description: Undecided blocks: if non-empty, submit does not proceed.

tools.name: review_health
tools.description: Local oversight signals for THIS session (GUARDRAILS.md §4): grounding coverage, forbidden evaluative language, and the correction/acceptance ratio. Read-only, no side effects, no network. Deliberately excludes anything that would measure the reviewer (time-in-tool, streaks) — not a verdict on the code or the human.

ungrounded_blocks.description: Blocks with zero citations. Should always be 0 — BlockGuard rejects an ungrounded block at construction (G2); a non-zero value signals a regression, not a normal finding.

evaluative_language_hits.description: Occurrences of the rubric's forbidden verdict vocabulary (G4) across all explanations in the session.

correction_rate_pct.description: corrections / (accepted + corrections). Null when nothing is decided yet — not 0%.

note.description: Always present: reframes the signals as being about the review's construction, never a judgment of the code or the reviewer.

forbidden_tools.description: Tools that MUST NOT exist: the AI neither judges nor decides correctness. The outcome comes only from accept_block/request_correction (human) + an explicit confirmation in submit_review.
